newsitem.title: USA: Host deal may generate $55.2 mln 97 EBITDA.
newsitem.headline: Host deal may generate $55.2 mln 97 EBITDA.

text.p: Host Marriott Corp said Tuesday its pact to buy 29 retirement communites, or all of Forum Group Inc, from Marriott Senior Living Services would generate about $55.2 million of 1997 Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization(EBITDA).
The deal would also make Host Marriott one of the five largest owners of real estate in the senior living industry.

Host Marriott said upon closing, the Forum transaction would bring the aggregate value of Host Marriott's 1997 year-to-date acquisitions to over $800 million, which is 80 percent of Host Marriott's 1997 acquisition goal of $1 billion.
Host Marriott will pay approximately $433 million for the existing portfolio of senior living communities and has established a $107 million expansion plan for the 29 retirement communities.

The aggregate $800 million includes $44 million of the expansion plan. The EBITDA figure is exclusive of the incremental EBITDA expected to be produced by the expansion plan of the Forum Group Portfolio. The expansion plan will add 1,075 units and is expected to be completed by January 1999.

Of the $107 million expansion plan, it is estimated that units with a value of $44 million will be completed prior to closing. The transaction, which is subject to the completion of due diligence and other customary closing conditions, is expected to close in the second quarter of 1997.

Terrence C. Golden, president and chief executive officer of Host Marriott said the acquisition from Marriott International Inc would "enable us to invest in an industry enjoying double digit growth rates, expand our alliance with Marriott International, further leverage off the benefits of the outstanding reputation of the Marriott brand, and diversify into an industry with cash flows that are independent of the business cycle."

Host Marriott said the senior living industry is expected to grow at an annual rate approaching 20 percent into the next decade and the over-85 age group is projected to double between the years 1990 and 2010. It said 25 percent of the over-85 population lives in "senior living facilities."

Of the $433 million Host Marriott will pay for the existing Forum Group portfolio, approximately $244 million is comprised of debt -- $229 million at fixed rates -- and the rest is cash. The transaction is subject to approval by its board of directors and a fairness opinion from its financial advisor.
